question: How are the junctions of the heart-lotus petals identified with external sites?
premises: The junctions of the heart-lotus petals form an octad of sub-clusters.
Jālandhara, Naipāla, Kaśmīra, Gargikā, and Hara are named in this context.
These names are correlated with the petal junctions.
inference: The octad of sub-clusters at the heart-lotus petal junctions is identified with specific external sites including Jālandhara, Naipāla, Kaśmīra, Gargikā, and Hara.
uncertainties: Only five names appear in this verse while an octad is indicated; the remaining three may follow in adjacent verses or be implied.
plain_english: At the junctions of the heart-lotus petals there is an octad of sub-clusters: Jālandhara, Naipāla, Kaśmīra, Gargikā, and Hara.
